annotations.text:
THE OVERLAND, AND WHAT IS INSIDE A PLACE
The rail carries only what is true wherever you are standing: Map, Tome, Defend, Party, Journal, Console. Brief, quests and boss are not destinations - they are aspects of an area, so they live inside one. Having “Quests” in the rail implied you could be in Quests without being anywhere.

The top row is the drill-down: the overland, then a place, then the work, then the boss. Map stays lit across all four, because that is how you got there.

THE AREA SCREEN
One page holding the three things about this place: what it teaches, the five quests, and the boss. The brief points at the Tome rather than trying to teach in a card - a paragraph in a panel is not instruction.

The challenge run sits in the sidebar on purpose. It is a legal opening move, not a reward for finishing.

MEDALS, DATAMINE, AND A SUBMIT THAT READS THE CODE
Unearned medal slots render greyed but present. Datamine gets its own panel because it is a modifier, not a medal, so it has no slot.

Submit actually parses the editor. The starter indexes inventory[block] directly, so a missing block raises KeyError instead of answering False - it fails until you handle the absent key with .get() or a membership test. Two failures open the Datamine.

SCARS (§5.3, §3.5)
Failed attempts listed with what actually went wrong, newest first, never collapsed behind a toggle. Four attempts on a boss is not a bad record - it is the record.

THE TOME — where the learning lives, and it expands in place
The gap this closes: §2.2 concedes gamification has “minimal impact on competency”, and the spec's answer is that building things teaches — which assumed he already knew what a dict was when he opened The Recipe Book. The only instruction was a brief per quest, which is the fragmentation, plus session plans living nowhere near the app.

Dense on purpose, open on purpose. Nothing here unlocks: a Tome that only opened what he had met would break the challenge run, which §5.2 says may be taken cold on pre-knowledge. And scanning a dense page for what you need is the actual skill.

IT IS NOT A POP-OVER. Opening it pushes the work down the page rather than covering it, so there is no layer to be inside and no escape convention to learn — “Open Tome” simply becomes “Close Tome”. The seam at the bottom shows the quest still sitting there rather than promising it. That also answers the case an overlay could not: clicking Tome in the rail with nothing open. There is always something underneath, even if it is the map, because expanding is a layout change and not a modal.

Authoring rule: it teaches the language, never the quest. dict gets inventory[“coal”], never can_craft — otherwise the reference is a solutions manual and Datamine stops meaning anything.

THE INVASION LADDER - ruled 2026-08-28
1, 3, 7, 16, 35 days. Repel one and it climbs a rung, so it stays away longer. Miss one and it steps back exactly one rung, never to the beginning.

That last clause is the decision. Resetting a well-known concept to day one punishes a single bad evening and then floods the next sessions with material he already had - which is the flaw this mechanic was built to prevent, reintroduced by its own scoring. Implemented and mutation-tested in packages/engine/src/invasions.ts.

A MEDAL THAT PAYS NOTHING SAYS “BRAG” - ruled 2026-08-28
Effective DC is clamped to the 5-30 scale, so at the floor a negative modifier is absorbed and the difference a medal pays really is 0. Rendering +0 XP reads as a broken app.

The chip says brag instead: honest about the payout, accurate about what the medal is worth, and true to what medals were always for - only Cleared was ever load-bearing. “Optional” was considered and dropped, because every medal but Cleared is already optional, so the word distinguishes nothing.

The engine still returns only the number. That a 0 becomes a word is a presentation decision, the same boundary §5.1 draws for the DC warning. The Recipe Book is DC 12, so no medal here pays 0 - faking one to show the chip would misrepresent the mechanic, so the rule lives in the logic.

THE JOURNAL — begins week 1, not week 3
§5.6 requires him to re-read his own entries from the start of an area before every boss, and calls that the strongest evidence a learner will ever get that he is not stupid. Entries starting in week 3 leave almost nothing to re-read before Boss 1, so the section was undercutting its own best mechanic.

The git half still arrives at Area 2a on schedule. Until then entries are plain markdown, and the Area 0 and 1 entries become the first real commit in his repository — a better first commit than an empty one.

Ten XP an entry, paid for substance rather than existence: the third prompt here is empty and says so. The DM replies to every one, which matters more than the scoring.

CONVENTIONS THESE SCREENS COMMIT TO

ONE LEXICON, EVERYWHERE. Patrol → Invasion. Muster → Defend. Chronicle → Journal. Board → Party. Tier → Area. Renamed through spec, content schema, engine, curriculum and UI — at Boss 7 he opens the engine repository and reads area: 3 in the YAML, and it should be the word he has said out loud all year.

BREADCRUMBS ARE THE NAVIGATION. Any screen reached through another shows the full trail, every ancestor clickable, the current page plain: Map › Area 3 · Collections › Quests › The Recipe Book. It is the only way back, so no screen can be one he enters and cannot leave except through browser chrome. A crumb names the activity, not the object — “Quests” answers why he would click it.

LABELS NEVER CHANGE WITH STATE. “Find the Boss” and “Take the Boss” read true whether he has cleared none of the quests or four. “Take it cold” was already false on a screen showing three cleared.
